The lead over epochs — tc1536 ÷ other − 1 · light = raw epoch, solid = on 5-epoch means · below 0 = tc1536 better

The −60% lead at ep 0–1 is the early dip; the raymap lead over tc128 widened to −15% by ep 70.

On raymap the tc128 gap was within 2% at ep 22–27, except ep 24 (−6.4%). It reached −13.8% at ep 35, narrowed to −1.8% at ep 50, and is −15.0% at ep 70. Against tc512 (to ep 59) pointmap and raymap stay below zero throughout; depth goes +0.3% to +1.6% at ep 5–7.

The tokenizer ceiling — *_tok = the GT delta code rolled out and decoded through the same frozen tokenizer, same 128 seqs

The depth win is mostly the tokenizer's ceiling; pointmap and raymap keep ~19% over tc128 after subtracting it.

The tc1536 tokenizer decodes the ground-truth code better than tc128 on all three losses, most on depth (2.63 vs 2.78). Subtracting each run's own ceiling leaves the part of the loss the flow is responsible for.

Findings

Full width trains and wins at N = 20. Whether it wins best-against-best needs a step sweep.

1
It trains, and was still improving at the wall. LossFlow 0.780 → 0.497 over ep 0–70, no NaN, flat since ep ~25. Pointmap and raymap kept falling: 8.17 / 5.70 at ep 39–43, 7.72 / 5.18 at ep 66–70.
2
It beats both at matched epoch. Ep 66–70 against tc128: depth −4.3%, pointmap −12.0%, raymap −15.0%. Ep 55–59 against tc512: −7.1% / −13.6% / −15.4%.
3
It is well past tc128's best. tc128's lowest 5-epoch window in 100 epochs is ep 40–44 (pointmap 8.69, raymap 6.02); tc1536 at ep 66–70 is 11.1% and 13.8% under it. tc128 then drifts up to 9.16 / 6.42 by ep 99.
4
Depth is mostly the tokenizer; pointmap and raymap are the flow. Above each ceiling at ep 66–70, tc1536 vs tc128 is depth −1.7%, pointmap −18.3%, raymap −19.6%.
5
It reverses the 2026-08-18 tc sweep, which ranked tc1536 worst. That flow (BSC:44543763) read pointmap 14.9 / raymap 13.5 at 3.2 M samples; this one reads 9.0 / 6.6 at the same count. Different tokenizer (SIGReg 0.005, pool 8192, ep 48) and batch 32, so not matched.
Caveat · steps. Every number here is N = 20. The tc128 and tc512 flows read best at N = 1–2 offline (tc512 raymap 4.58 at N = 2 vs 6.38 at N = 20). Nothing says tc1536 keeps its lead there.
Caveat · tokenizer. Not a pure width ablation: bottleneck, SIGReg weight, pool, warmup and decoder noise also differ (slide 02). tc1536 reads epoch_30, the others epoch_100.
Caveat · MSEToken. It is in each tokenizer's own z units and ranks the widths opposite to every decoded loss. It was not normalised by code variance.
Caveat · one seed per arm, and the 128 eval sequences are fixed across epochs.
Frames barely show the win; camera paths do (slides 06–07). At each run's last epoch, t4 depth error against own GT-z is 2.23 / 2.31 / 2.21 m (tc128 / tc512 / tc1536) and RGB error 11.7 / 11.6 / 11.3. Every flow overshoots the GT camera path; mean path error on the 6 moving scenes is 9.4 / 6.7 / 4.8 m (tc1536: 7.3 m at ep 43).
Not done. No step sweep (iter_100000 lands at ep 50). The run was not chained: the 48 h wall stopped it at ep 70 of 100.
